name: kerryback

plugins.name: litdb
plugins.description: Personal literature + notes knowledge base: hybrid keyword+semantic search over your papers and notes, Zotero/Better BibTeX import, loose-PDF folder ingestion with full text, OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar discovery, and a citation graph. Local-first; the runtime installs into ~/.litdb on first use.

plugins.name: finance-data
plugins.description: Fetch free financial, market, and economic data (prices, fundamentals, SEC filings, macro series, asset-pricing factors) from Yahoo, Stooq, SEC EDGAR, FRED, Ken French, FinnHub, FMP, and US Treasury, and save it as CSV.

plugins.name: wrds
plugins.description: Empirical asset-pricing data from WRDS (CRSP v2/Compustat) and Open Source Asset Pricing: extractable Python building blocks for connect (without a 2FA prompt), pull, merge, market cap aggregated across share classes, the CRSP-Compustat link, book equity, accounting alignment and firm age — every query run against live WRDS. Surfaces the constructions that are genuine decisions rather than common practice (Ken French vs Drechsler's WRDS script vs OpenAP, and the 4- vs 6-month reporting lag) instead of picking silently, and ships twelve WRDS reference scripts.

plugins.name: two-stage-dcf
plugins.description: Two-stage enterprise valuation from staged financial statements and company text. Classifies every reported balance-sheet line and foots it, computes the historical driver ratios with a script, reads the MD&A, transcripts and press releases for evidence on each driver, and writes two HTML pages: the argument for each assumption, with quoted citations and a measured ranking of what moves the answer, and the valuation it produces. The numbers live in a CSV that rebuilds both pages, so the assumptions can be argued over and revised; when they are settled it delivers an Excel workbook whose model is live formulas, with sensitivity and driver-ranking sheets and a Check sheet that goes red if the formulas ever disagree with the Python engine.

description: Research data and valuation skills for Claude Code: a personal literature and notes knowledge base, free financial and economic data, empirical asset-pricing data from WRDS, and two-stage DCF enterprise valuation.
